senses.gloss:
Nai-dāgha is the name of the ‘summer’ season in the later
Saṃhitās and Brāhmaṇas.^1 Cf. Ṛtu and Nidāgha.
1) Av. ix. 5, 31; Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa,
i. 8, 4, 2; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, i. 4,
1, 16, etc.; naidāghīya, ‘belonging to
the summer,’ Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa,
xxiii. 16, 8, etc.

Nai-dāna is a term applied in the Nirukta^1 to a class of
Vedic interpreters. Roth^2 takes the Naidānas to be ‘etymo-
logists,’ but Sieg^3 thinks they are the same as the Aitihāsikas
or ‘legendarists.’^4
1) vi. 9; vii. 12.
2) St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v. But
of. Nirukta, Erlāuterungen, 220, 221;
Muir, Sanskrit Texts, 2^2, 176.
3) Die Sagenstoffe des Ṛgveda, 29.
4) The word seems to mean ‘one
concerned with the original form’
(nidāna).
